doc.title: Jimmy Heath — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Travel hassles and fifty years of marriage to Mona
summary: Heath complains about travel, praises his marriage and his parents, and drifts to Obama's single-parent upbringing.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: How much of the year are you on the road?
Well, you know, it’s not as much as one would think but it’s enough.
How do you feel about the travel part?
The travel is getting ridiculous because they…
In the 9-11 world it’s a different story than it was in ’95.

And they bother you about your instruments! Now, my wife, who I will have been married to…well we met over 50 years ago in May of ’59 so Feburary the 4th we will be married 50 years. So Mona goes on the gigs with me just to take one of the horns (Laughs). They don’t want me to bring two on board the plane. That’s her excuse, she’s like an American Express card, I never leave home without her. I mean, 50 years man! That’s like a family, as role models, my mom and pop were together like that. Percy was together 50 years with his wife. Tootie has been together with two wives about 35 years or more. I can’t imagine people not having both of their parents. I feel so special to have had both of my parents. I tore my butt and made them mad, and cried, and all that. They would always accept me back, prodigal son. But to have one parent and to make something of yourself Alan Witchcomb did it, Obama.
